rounds.text: Onix Solar Energy Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum, driven by a phenomenal compounded sales growth of 463% and an astonishing compounded profit growth of 2071% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This explosive fundamental growth is supported by quarter-over-quarter sales increases [E54] and a favorable macro backdrop, with the company operating in a sector characterized by a strong tailwind score of +0.88 alongside robust sector median sales growth of 25.9% and profit growth of 34.3% [E59, E60, E61, E62]. The business is conservatively financed with an exceptionally low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x and comfortable short-term liquidity featuring a current ratio of 7.44x [E27, E28, E48]. Furthermore, long-term investors have been rewarded by strong historical compounding, evidenced by share price growth of 112% over 5 years and 106% over 3 years [E17, E18], while insiders have demonstrated significant conviction as promoter holdings increased by 20.84 percentage points to 50.22% from Sep 2023 to Jun 2026 [E31]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -236 Cr in Mar 2026 resulting in a cash conversion ratio of -7.61x [E23, E24].

The business is severely overvalued according to multiple valuation models, with a discounted cash flow estimating intrinsic value at Rs 191 per share against a market price of Rs 340, leaving a negative margin of safety of -77.9% [E34, E35]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price already prices in an aggressive 17.9% earnings growth rate, surpassing the 10.0% assumed in the base case [E36]. Operational execution reveals massive cash flow deterioration, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -236 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -236 Cr in March 2026, translating to a distressing cash conversion of -7.61x [E23, E24, E25]. Working capital pressures are mounting heavily as debtor days stretch to 262 days and working capital requirements explode from 148 days to 494 days [E51, E52]. Technical momentum is completely broken, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, sitting at a relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500, and culminating in an overall rules-based screen score of just 29 out of 100 which triggers a SELL rating with low confidence [E39, E40, E53]. conceded: [E14]

While the bear highlights a discounted cash flow valuation pointing to Rs 191, the business trades at an attractive price-to-book of 1.56x against its sector benchmark of 2.2x and boasts a strong ROA of 7.46% that beats the sector benchmark of 5.29% [E2, E7, E8]. On operational momentum, profit growth of 2071% outpaces 1-year price growth by 1,997%, indicating that profit expansion is rapidly beginning to outperformance expectations [E15, E46]. Regarding balance sheet health, the company remains conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x and comfortable short-term liquidity backed by a current ratio of 7.44x [E27, E28]. Although the bear flags short-term cash flow pressures and lagging technicals, promoter commitment has strengthened significantly with promoter holding rising by 20.84 percentage points to reach 50.22% [E31]. Furthermore, the company benefits from operating within a strong sector tailwind in Metals & Mining carrying a robust tailwind score of +0.88 alongside sector median sales growth of 25.9% [E60, E62]. conceded: [E24, E34, E39, E40]

The bull cites an attractive price-to-book ratio of 1.56x against the sector benchmark of 2.2x [E7], but this ignores a rich P/E of 27.7x and a DCF intrinsic value of only Rs 191 that leaves a massive -77.9% margin of safety against the current Rs 340 price [E1, E34, E35, E58]. While the bull points to strong ROA and profit growth [E8, E15], the company suffers from a severely negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -236 Cr in Mar 2026, meaning cash conversion collapses to -7.61x against reported profits [E23, E24, E25, E26]. Furthermore, the bull's emphasis on promoter commitment [E31] overlooks negative flags that promoter holding actually decreased over the last quarter by -24.8% [E50]. The bull highlights a conservative debt-to-equity ratio [E27], but borrowings surged from Rs 0 Cr to Rs 57 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside alarming working capital strains, as high debtors reach 262 days and working capital days balloon from 148 days to 494 days [E29, E51, E52]. Finally, conceded: [E2, E60, E62].
